title: Valid Palindrome
statement: You get a piece of text. Ignore every character that is not a letter or a digit, and ignore upper or lower case. Say whether what is left reads the same forwards and backwards. Empty text counts as a palindrome.

example.caption: Without the space, the exclamation mark and the capital, the text is nursesrun. It reads the same both ways.

idea.sentence: Compare the two ends and walk inward. If the ends always match, the middle can only be fine, so no reversed copy is needed.

jargon.plain: Text that reads the same from left to right and from right to left.
A letter or a digit. Spaces and punctuation are not.

watch.inputHint: One argument: the text in quotes, e.g. "Nurses run!"

rows.name: Clean and reverse
rows.note: Build a cleaned string, reverse it, compare. Simple, but it stores copies.

rows.name: Two pointers
rows.note: Each pointer moves at most n times in total. Only two integers are kept.

fast.takeaway: Both are one pass. The pointers do the cleaning on the fly, so there is nothing extra to store.

stages.title: Ends
stages.note: l starts at the first character and r at the last.

stages.title: Skip junk
stages.note: Move a pointer past spaces and punctuation until it sits on a letter or digit.

stages.title: Compare
stages.note: Lower-case both characters and compare. A difference means the answer is false.

stages.title: Move inward
stages.note: The pair matched, so step l right and r left.

stages.title: All matched
stages.note: The pointers met without a mismatch. Return true.

edges.title: Empty text
edges.why: r starts at -1, so the loop never runs. Nothing to compare means it passes.

edges.title: Only punctuation
edges.why: Both pointers skip until they meet. After cleaning the text is empty.

edges.title: Digit against letter
edges.why: The trick of adding 32 to lower-case a code also turns the digit 0 into the letter P. Only lower-case real letters.

edges.title: One character
edges.why: l and r start on the same index. A single character mirrors itself.

gotchas.text: s[i] is a byte, not a character. Scanning bytes is safe here only because we count ASCII letters and digits. Every byte of a multi-byte character is above 127, so it is skipped. To keep accented letters you would convert to []rune first.
There is no built-in lower-case for a single byte. Write one (add 32 for A to Z), or use unicode.ToLower on a rune.
s[i] and s.length count UTF-16 code units. Emoji and some scripts take two units, which is another reason this solution defines letters as ASCII only.
Do not build the regex with a global flag (/x/g) and reuse it. A global regex keeps lastIndex between test() calls and gives wrong answers.
Check l < r again inside each skip loop. Without it a run of punctuation can push a pointer off the end of the text.

recap.pattern: Two pointers: meet in the middle
recap.key: Start at both ends, skip junk, compare, step inward. One mismatch decides the answer.
moves: l at the start, r at the end
Skip characters that are not letters or digits
Compare lower-cased characters; a difference means false
Move both inward until they meet
